Which celebrity have you personally met and found to be the most down-to-earth person?
When I was 7 years old I went to disney world and Beetlejuice signed my autograph book. it was awesome. 10/10 highly recommend.

Gabe Newell. I was first to an outhouse at Oregon Raceway Park. Being a little bit of a fan boy all I could blurt out was "Sorry about that." He responded with something along the lines of "Don't worry about it." I was going to ask him for a picture but I really just wanted him to feel like there was a place he could just be a normal person and not have to worry about all the fan fair.

Andy Dalton, QB for the Cincinnati Bengals, is genuinely one of the nicest, most down-to-earth people on this planet. He's the classic good Christian Texan that actually practices what he preaches. He pretty much spends all his spare time with his wife and child doing hands-on work for their charity foundation, which has brought a ton of joy to children and their parents. They recently started to hold a "date night" every year for the parents of very ill children, giving them a rare night out when their children normally require around-the-clock care. A family friend actually was invited to it last year because her child was waiting on a lung transplant, and she still tears up when she talks about how wonderful what Andy did for her was.

Sort-of related: When I had some one-on-one time with him years ago, when we were finished talking, he called over the Ben-Gal cheerleaders and took a photo of me with them. And THEN the cheerleaders gave me their signed swimsuit calendar. I love that guy.
I've waited on James Woods a number of times. Despite what many people say about him, he seemed awfully decent to me.

I met Brad Pitt 17 years ago. We spoke for about 5 minutes, shared a few jokes. Seemed like any other person you would have a casual conversation with.

John Goodman also came through a drive-thru/diner I worked at when I was 18. It was after the bars closed, he was a little tipsy, we were slow, and pretty much everyone working that night got autographs.

I met Brian Posehn at a comic signing before his stand up show. Seemed like a really great guy, shot the shit with me for five minutes or so about music and our kids. Really laid back and down to earth. Also did a meet and greet with Rival Sons a couple years ago. They seemed really down to earth. Jay (the singer) even made time to chat with me about their recording process in the parking lot as we were leaving (he was walking out at the same time).

A bunch of us metalheads from a small town in Alberta, Canada went on a road trip to see Slayer and Pantera play. After the show we wanted to see if we could get some autographs so we went to the back of the stadium and waited for the band to exit the show.

Kerry King and Dimebag Darrell were rock stars, had girls and security all around them and left promptly. But Jeff Hanneman came out to the bus and greeted us all, had a beer and smoked a some weed with us while signing anything we would put in front of him. We all got hats and shirts signed, the girls got their tits signed and a couple of guys got their heads signed. He was an all around cool dude. He must have been out there for over an hour before he said he had to leave and meet up with the rest of the band. It was awesome!
